newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire says no Chinese troops in Kinshasa.
newsitem.headline: Zaire says no Chinese troops in Kinshasa.

text.p: Zaire on Tuesday dismissed as "propaganda" allegations by rebels that Chinese soldiers had arrived in the capital Kinshasa to help repulse a feared attack by rebels trying to topple President Mobutu Sese Seko.

"There is no Chinese soldier in Zaire to help the FAZ (Zaire army). It is not true," Leon Kalima, spokesman for emergency rule Prime Minister Likulia Bolongo, told Reuters. "It is pure propaganda. The rebels are waging a psychological war."
China itself has dismissed the report as "groundless".

Rebel "finance minister" Mawana Nanga Mawampanga said in the southern city of Lubumbashi that Chinese troops were in Kinshasa. "We know of 400 troops at present," he added, reading a statement from rebel leader Laurent Kabila.
A senior Chinese army general met Mobutu at his jungle palace in Gbadolite, northern Zaire, in January just over two months after rebels took up arms in the east in October.
The visit, whose clear purpose was not explained officially, sparked speculation in the local press that China could help Zaire's beleaguered army to crush the rebellion.

The rebels now hold half of Zaire but Bolongo said on Monday that the army had sufficient firepower to beat back any rebel attack on the capital, the remaining stronghold of Mobutu's forces and home to more than five million people.
Kalima said there was little Chinese soldiers could do to help. "What Zaire needs is moral and logistical support. I do not know if the Chinese can provide that," he said.
